subject.title: Windows: multiple gateway-down failure modes (kill-and-rebind restart loop, config-edit no-relaunch, browser launch crash, blocking pricing fetches)

question: Should this issue remain the canonical Windows gateway-down umbrella while maintainers split separate fixes for lifecycle, invalid-config repair, browser isolation, pricing readiness, and CLI shim behavior?
rationale: The report combines credible failures across stable gateway lifecycle, CLI config repair, browser plugin runtime, and pricing behavior; the correct fix order and recovery UX require maintainer ownership rather than one automated patch.

options.title: Keep Umbrella And Split Fixes
options.body: Use this issue as the incident tracker and create or link narrow fixes for each proven sub-boundary, starting with idempotent gateway ensure and invalid-config repair.

options.title: Require Live Windows Proof First
options.body: Pause implementation until a maintainer or reporter captures process, listener, browser, and startup timing proof for the highest-risk paths.

options.title: Close Fixed Sub-Branches Later
options.body: After proving specific subproblems are fixed on main or shipped, close or redirect only those branches while keeping unresolved failures tracked elsewhere.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella And Split Fixes
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the incident tracker and create or link narrow fixes for each proven sub-boundary, starting with idempotent gateway ensure and invalid-config repair.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest current-history signal across the gateway lifecycle, stale-process cleanup, pricing, and browser launch surfaces touched by the umbrella.
